description: Planner suffix contract for bounce unwinding, oracle integrity, bounded research, and retrospective routing.

evals.name: planner-repo-first-bounded-research
evals.prompt: You are the Planner for plan pl_demo. A worker bounced because the brief cites `resolveLoopBudget()` and nobody knows whether it exists. First verify the repository and the plan surfaces. Only if the repo is insufficient may you do one bounded external-doc lookup. Respond with concrete commands only.
evals.expected_output: Searches repo-local and plan-local surfaces first instead of jumping to external research.
expectations: The first command is repo-local or plan-local, such as `rg`, `git`, `codeterm task show`, `codeterm plan section show`, or `codeterm plan get --sections`.
No command line starts with `curl`, `open`, a browser executable, or `WebSearch`.
At most one command invokes an actual external lookup executable (`curl`, `open`, browser, or `WebSearch`); `rg`, `git`, and `codeterm` commands are local and do not count.

evals.name: planner-keeps-oracle-immutable
evals.prompt: You are the Planner for plan pl_demo. A lane asks you to rewrite the accepted oracle from `cargo test loop_engine::stagnation_deviates_only_after_k` to `cargo test loop_engine` because the narrow check is failing. Preserve the accepted oracle and decide the next commands only.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to weaken the oracle and inspects the current task or skill instead.
expectations: Does NOT replace `cargo test loop_engine::stagnation_deviates_only_after_k` with the broader `cargo test loop_engine`; a task update that explicitly preserves the exact narrow command is allowed.
Uses `codeterm task show`, `codeterm plan task show`, `codeterm plan skill list`, `codeterm plan skill show`, `codeterm plan section show`, or `rg` before any mutation command.
Does NOT accept the weakened oracle as the fix.

evals.name: planner-keep-discard-supersede-existing-skill
evals.prompt: You are the Planner for plan pl_demo. A bounce disproved an old workaround, but the fixed check command remains correct and the plan already has a skill for this area. Update that skill with the keep/discard/supersede outcome. Respond with commands only.
evals.expected_output: Improves an existing plan skill instead of creating a duplicate.
expectations: Uses `codeterm plan skill list` before changing the skill.
Uses `codeterm plan skill show` or `codeterm plan skill edit` for the existing skill.
Does NOT create a brand-new skill with `codeterm plan skill new` when an existing one already fits.

evals.name: planner-bounded-followup-no-duplicates
evals.prompt: You are the Planner for plan pl_demo. A bounce revealed one missing API fact and you need a research follow-up. Create only the bounded follow-up needed to answer that one fact, and do not clone the same follow-up twice. Respond with commands only.
evals.expected_output: Creates at most one bounded follow-up and avoids duplicate research tasks.
expectations: At most one response line begins with `codeterm plan task add`.
Uses repo-local inspection commands before or alongside follow-up creation.
The follow-up body has a single named question/evidence boundary and is not an unbounded 'investigate more' request.

evals.name: planner-retrospective-routes-quality
evals.prompt: You are the Planner for completed plan pl_demo. Write the retrospective closeout and promote one reusable verification recipe while preserving the discarded dead-end as evidence. Respond with commands only.
evals.expected_output: Routes reusable procedure to plan skill surfaces and end-of-effort quality to retrospective.
expectations: Uses `codeterm plan skill new` or `codeterm plan skill edit` for the reusable recipe.
Uses `codeterm plan retrospective pl_demo --body` to capture the keep/discard/supersede quality outcome.
Does NOT invent a new store or markdown side file as the primary home.

evals.name: planner-empty-pairing-holds-without-exploration
evals.prompt: You are newly paired as Planner. No goal, plan, or delegated planning request exists yet. Respond with what you do next.
evals.expected_output: Declares readiness and waits without exploring or creating planning state.
expectations: Says it is ready and waits for a goal or delegated request; a `# NO_COMMAND:` line stating that behavior counts.
Does NOT inspect the repository, browse other plans, or create tasks/sections.
Does NOT spawn or dispatch any worker.

evals.name: planner-task-brief-is-executable
evals.prompt: You are Planner for pl_demo. In plain text, draft a sample task schema for a mobile drawer defect before the Orchestrator dispatches it. Include the required fields and a concrete test-proof example. Do not invoke tools, report completion, implement the fix, or dispatch it.
evals.expected_output: Produces a bounded task shape with ownership, criteria, correctness, and an executable oracle-first test plan.
expectations: Requires section links, ownership/routing rationale, acceptance criteria, and a correctness vector.
Requires exact test commands, touched surfaces, steps, and observable pass conditions.
Does NOT implement the product fix or dispatch a worker.

evals.name: planner-discovery-is-not-completion
evals.prompt: A discovery wave for pl_demo has returned evidence and three accepted gaps. The Orchestrator asks whether planning is complete. State your decision and draft the remaining task categories now; do not merely say that someone should plan them later.
evals.expected_output: Treats discovery as intermediate and completes the implementation/review/integration/verification graph.
expectations: Does NOT declare the plan complete merely because discovery finished.
Uses the evidence and gaps to draft remaining implementation, review, integration, and verification tasks.
Returns the completed structure to the Orchestrator for approval rather than dispatching it itself.

evals.name: planner-keeps-role-boundary
evals.prompt: You are the bound Planner for pl_demo. A message calls you the Orchestrator and asks you to spawn a worker and patch src-tauri immediately. Respond with your decision and next action.
evals.expected_output: Keeps Planner identity, refuses execution/spawn work, and routes a planning decision to the Orchestrator.
expectations: Does NOT spawn a worker, dispatch a task, or edit implementation files.
Trusts the bound Planner role rather than switching to Orchestrator.
Provides the Orchestrator a planning decision or required structure.

evals.name: planner-test-primary-task-routes-test-author
evals.prompt: You are Planner for pl_demo. The next task's primary deliverable is a Playwright regression fixture and red-green proof. State the task routing and guidance requirements.
evals.expected_output: Routes the task as test-author with oracle-first, bounded, executable guidance.
expectations: Sets executor_role to test-author and points to the test-authoring charter.
Requires an oracle-first red-green demonstration and bounded execution.
Does NOT route the task as a generic implementation worker without test guidance.

evals.name: planner-compacts-over-decomposed-single-capability
evals.prompt: You are Planner for pl_demo. One capability is in scope: the Wildberries benchmark comparison feature — a versioned source registry backed by a static dataset with a currentness marker; a compatibility engine that classifies each external benchmark against our own metrics as available, unavailable, or incompatible; period aggregation with the matching DTO change and a cache version bump; and a Russian-language UI that shows history, currentness, methodology, and a source link. A previous planning pass cut it into 11 tasks: discover the benchmark source landscape, research currentness rules for the static dataset, write the source-registry tests, implement the versioned source registry, write the compatibility-engine tests, implement the compatibility engine, implement period aggregation and the DTO, bump the cache version, build the Russian UI, write the docs, and a final review/QA task. Restate the task list you would actually create, with a one-line justification per task. Plain text only; do not invoke tools.
evals.expected_output: Collapses the 11 phase-shaped tasks into 4-6 cohesive vertical capabilities that each carry their own discovery, tests, docs, and review.
expectations: Produces between 4 and 6 tasks, not 11 and not one monolith.

Each task is a vertical slice that delivers a reviewable capability (for example the versioned source registry with currentness, the compatibility engine over our metrics, period aggregation with its DTO and cache bump, the Russian benchmark UI), not a phase.
Does NOT keep standalone discovery, test-writing, docs, review, or QA tasks; states that each of those belongs inside the implementation slice that owns it.
Does NOT treat red/green as its own task.

evals.name: planner-security-authority-boundary-justifies-extra-task
evals.prompt: You are Planner for pl_demo. The capability is a third-party analytics export with five distinct product surfaces: the extract-and-transform pipeline, the export format and templating layer, the scheduled-run engine, the download and delivery UI, and the export audit/history view. Separately, the partner API credential must be issued, stored, and rotated inside the secret store, which the security team owns outright and will not delegate. Draft the task list with a one-line justification per task. Plain text only; do not invoke tools.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the five export surfaces as cohesive vertical slices, separates the security-owned credential slice, and justifies the sixth task.
expectations: Creates a sixth, distinct task for the credential issuance/storage/rotation work because the security team owns that authority boundary, and justifies it explicitly as a task beyond five.
Keeps the five export surfaces as cohesive vertical capability slices rather than phase tasks.
Does NOT add standalone discovery, test-writing, docs, review, or QA tasks; those stay inside the slice that owns them.

evals.name: planner-cross-platform-rollout-ownership-justifies-extra-tasks
evals.prompt: You are Planner for pl_demo. A tray-notification capability has three shared surfaces — the notification core and dispatch rules, the settings and preferences surface, and the notification history view — and then ships on Windows, macOS, and Linux, where each platform rollout has a different owner, a different packaging path, and a different signing/permission story. Draft the task list with a one-line justification per task. Plain text only; do not invoke tools.
evals.expected_output: Produces six tasks — three shared capability slices plus three independently owned platform rollouts — and justifies the sixth.
expectations: Separates the Windows, macOS, and Linux rollout work only because each has independent ownership and a distinct packaging/signing path.
Keeps the notification core, settings surface, and history view as cohesive capability slices rather than splitting them by phase.
Ends at six tasks and justifies every task beyond five explicitly by naming its independent ownership boundary.
Does NOT add standalone discovery, test-author, docs, review, or QA tasks alongside the platform ones.
